statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, len(r) = n, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, letting G_i = { j | i < j < n and nums[j] > nums[i] }: if |G_i| >= 2 and j1 is the least element of G_i and j2 is the least element of G_i with j2 > j1, then r[i] = nums[j2]; if |G_i| < 2, then r[i] = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, second_greater_element nums returns a result r; execution does not fail by overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, either r[i] = -1 or 0 <= r[i] <= 1000000000.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r[i] != -1 then r[i] > nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = -1 if and only if the number of indices j with i < j < n and nums[j] > nums[i] is less than 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r[i] != -1 then there exists an index j such that i < j < n, nums[j] = r[i], nums[j] > nums[i], and the number of indices k with i < k < j and nums[k] > nums[i] is exactly 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i and every j with 0 <= i < n, i < j < n, nums[j] > nums[i], and the number of indices k with i < k < j and nums[k] > nums[i] exactly 1, we have r[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever second_greater_element nums returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if there are at least two indices j with i < j < n and nums[j] > nums[i], and if j1 is the least such index and j2 is the least index satisfying j1 < j2 < n and nums[j2] > nums[i], then r[i] = nums[j2].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
